newsitem.title: USA: Grace posts $2.5 billion profit from spinoffs.
newsitem.headline: Grace posts $2.5 billion profit from spinoffs.

text.p: W. R. Grace & Co. said Tuesday it posted a $2.5 billion profit in the third quarter, primarily from the spinoffs of its medical subsidiary and some packaging and speciality chemicals businesses.

The company said that including special and one-time items in both periods, its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 was $2.52 billion, or $27.66 a share, compared with $21.7 million, or 22 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.

Grace said that $2.46 billion, or $27.05 a share, of the profit was income from discontinued operations. Otherwise, it said, third-quarter earnings from continuing operations expanded to $55.5 million, or 61 cents a share, from $19.8 million, or 20 cents a share.

The company, based in Boca Raton, Fla., said the increase in operating earnings was a result of an improved cost structure and strong performance from Grace's catalysts, silicas and construction products businesses.
Grace, which is seeking to become a dominant global supplier of packaging and speciality chemicals, said its sales in the third quarter fell to $821 million from $946 million.
The company said its income from packaging declined 2 percent on essentially flat revenues, compared with exceptionally strong results in the year-ago quarter.

Sales and earnings continued to be impacted by lower pork production in North America and by lower volumes of fresh red meat in Europe and Japan, as well as by competitive pressures in North America and Asia Pacific for display films used to package consumer goods.

However, Grace said that during the quarter it completed its acquisition of Cypress Packaging Inc., which positioned Grace Packaging as the leading supplier of pre-cut produce packaging in North America -- one of several key growth areas.
Grace said earnings from its catalysts and silicas business rose 12 percent and results for construction products were up sharply.
However, earnings from fluid cracking catalysts were depressed due to continuing weakness in the North American market and competitive pricing pressures, Grace said.
Grace's stock added 12.5 cents to $52.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
